summary: A 1966 cab on a 30-foot steel tower in the Modoc National Forest, on a summit approved for administrative use by 1912 and with fire-watch records from 1932 to 1945.

facts.design: CL-100 cab on a 30-foot K-brace steel tower
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Modoc National Forest

events.note: Site approved or withdrawn for administrative use; NHLR says a platform lookout may have stood here as early as 1912
Otto W. Klosterman named as the lookout in an August 1932 newspaper item quoted by the history site
Fire spread over about 6,000 acres of grass, sage and juniper; radio contact was established between fire fighters and the lookout
Damon's Butte Road Fire first reported from the lookout at 6:05 a.m. on October 2, 1945
Current CL-100 cab completed on a 30-foot K-brace steel tower

notes_for_editor: No page I could read says whether Timber Mountain is staffed now or open to climbing, so the story says so and no access or staffing keys are set. A search snippet hinted at Forest Service staffing and a 2022 blog visit, but snippets were not read pages and are not used. The 1912 platform is 'may have' per NHLR only. The 1932-1945 history comes from one compiled history site quoting newspapers and Forest Service records; not checked against originals. The 30-foot height is the NHLR's tower height; the total height of the cab on it is not given. The brief's build year (1966) and elevation check out.
